body.claim: Documentation describes what is, never what changed: no temporal framing, no narration of the document itself, no slogans or rhetorical summary beats, and headings that name a subject.
body.detail: Three classes, all of which shipped and had to be removed. Temporal and indirect-temporal framing is prose whose referent is a prior state — "this is a tool call rather than a command it types" explains an edit to a reader who never saw the version it replaced, and is the same defect as a comment reading "now using X instead of Y". Self-narration is the document describing its own structure, as in "the rest of this page is". Rhetorical beats are lines like "that is the whole idea", which summarise for effect rather than inform. The restriction is as strict as the no-comments rule and for the same reason: a reader arrives with no history, and prose that assumes one is prose they cannot use. Applies to README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md and docs/. Error messages and commit messages describe a change by nature and are exempt.
